MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Fragile X syndrome

TEST DESCRIPTION
PCR-based assay for CGG repeat expansion analysis in the FMR1 gene (FRAXA) and GCC repeat expansion analysis in the FMR2 gene (FRAXE). This test detects expansions in the promoter regions of both genes associated with Fragile X syndrome and FRAXE intellectual disability.

Methodology: PCR amplification with capillary electrophoresis for accurate sizing of CGG repeats in FMR1 and GCC repeats in FMR2. The assay can reliably detect normal, intermediate, premutation, and full mutation ranges.

RESULTS

FMR1 Gene Analysis (FRAXA)
CGG Repeat Size: 29 repeats
Interpretation: NORMAL RANGE

FMR2 Gene Analysis (FRAXE)
GCC Repeat Size: 16 repeats
Interpretation: NORMAL RANGE

No pathogenic expansions detected in either FMR1 or FMR2 genes.

SUMMARY
Molecular testing for Fragile X syndrome (FRAXA) and FRAXE-associated intellectual disability shows normal repeat sizes in both FMR1 and FMR2 genes. These results significantly reduce the likelihood of Fragile X syndrome to less than 1%.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
The absence of CGG expansion in FMR1 and GCC expansion in FMR2 makes the diagnosis of Fragile X syndrome or FRAXE-associated intellectual disability highly unlikely. However, it should be noted that rare cases (<1%) of Fragile X syndrome may be caused by point mutations, deletions, or other rearrangements within the FMR1 gene that are not detectable by this PCR-based expansion analysis.

TECHNICAL NOTES
Repeat Size Reference Ranges:

FMR1 (FRAXA):
- Normal: 5-44 CGG repeats
- Intermediate: 45-54 CGG repeats
- Premutation: 55-200 CGG repeats
- Full mutation: >200 CGG repeats

FMR2 (FRAXE):
- Normal: 6-30 GCC repeats
- Intermediate: 31-60 GCC repeats
- Full mutation: >200 GCC repeats

Test Limitations:
- This assay detects only CGG/GCC repeat expansions
- Point mutations, deletions, or rearrangements are not detected
- Mosaicism may affect interpretation
- Very large expansions may fail to amplify

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
